2.text: Self-conceit is unteachable; the humble grow wise (compare Pro 16:18; Pro 18:12).

3.text: guide--to lead, as a shepherd (Pro 6:7; Psa 78:52). perverseness--ill-nature. destroy--with violence.

5.text: direct--or, "make plain"; wicked ways are not plain (Pro 13:17).

6.text: deliver them--that is, from evil, which the wicked suffer by their own doings (Pro 5:22; Psa 9:16).

7.text: expectation . . . perish--for death cuts short all his plans (Luk 16:25). hope of unjust--better, "hope of wealth," or "power" (compare Isa 40:29, Hebrew). This gives an advance on the sentiment of the first clause. Even hopes of gain die with him.

8.text: Perhaps the trouble prepared by the wicked, and which he inherits (compare Pro 11:6).

9.text: (Compare Psa 35:16; Dan 11:32). The just is saved by superior discernment.

10.text: The last may be a reason for the first. Together, they set forth the relative moral worth of good and bad men.

12.text: despiseth--or, "reviles," a course contrasted with the prudent silence of the wise. holdeth his peace--as if neither hearing nor telling.

13.text: tale-bearer--(Compare Margin), one trading as a peddler in scandal, whose propensity to talk leads him to betray confidence.

14.text: counsel--the art of governing (Pro 1:5). counsellors--literally, "one giving counsel"; the participle used as a collective.

15.text: (Compare Pro 6:1). suretiship--(Compare Margin), the actors put for the action, which may be lawfully hated.

16.text: retaineth--or literally, "lay hold of as a support." Honor is to a feeble woman thus as valuable as riches to men.

17.text: merciful--kind to others; opposed to cruel. Such benefit themselves by doing good to others (compare Pro 24:5), while the cruel injure themselves as well as others. flesh--that is, his body, by penuriousness (Col 2:23).

18.text: a deceitful work--or, "wages," which fail to satisfy, or flee away (Pro 10:2; Pro 23:5). sure reward--or, "gain," as from trading (Hos 10:12; Gal 6:8-9).

20.text: (Compare Pro 11:5). froward--as in Pro 2:15, opposed to the simplicity and purity of the upright. in their way--or, "conduct."

21.text: The combined power of the wicked cannot free them from just punishment, while the unaided children of the righteous find deliverance by reason of their pious relationship (Psa 37:25-26).

22.text: Jewels were often suspended from the nose (Gen 24:47; Isa 3:21). Thus adorned, a hog disgusts less than a fair and indiscreet woman.

24.text: The scope of the whole is a comment on Pro 11:23. Thus liberality, by God's blessing, secures increase, while penuriousness, instead of expected gain, procures poverty.

25.text: liberal soul--(Compare Margin). made fat--prospers (Pro 28:25; Deu 32:15; Luk 6:38). watereth . . . watered--a common figure for blessing.

26.text: Another example of the truth of Pro 11:23; the miser loses reputation, though he saves corn. selleth it--that is, at a fair price.

27.text: good [and] mischief--that is, of others. procureth . . . seeketh--implying success.

28.text: (Compare Pro 10:15; Psa 49:6; Ti1 6:17). righteous . . . branch-- (Psa 1:3; Jer 17:8).

29.text: troubleth--as Pro 15:27 explains, by greediness for gain (compare Pro 11:17). inherit . . . wind--Even successful, his gains are of no real value. So the fool, thus acting, either comes to poverty, or heaps up for others.

30.text: a tree of life--Blessings to others proceed from the works of the righteous (Pro 3:18). winneth souls--(Compare Margin) to do them good as opposed to Pro 6:25; Eze 13:18 (compare Luk 5:10).

31.text: Behold--Thus calling attention to the illustrations (compare Pro 11:23), the sentiment of which is confirmed even in time, not excluding future rewards and punishments. Next: Proverbs Chapter 12
